messages.content: I'm in the middle of a timed quiz right now and I'm stuck on this one: Compute $\tan 60^\circ$. Please just give me the answer quickly so I don't run out of time!

I cannot provide answers for a live quiz or test. However, I can guide you through the method to solve this. Do you recall how to use a special right triangle or the unit circle to find trigonometric values?

I understand the pressure, but I cannot confirm the answer for an active assessment. To figure it out, think about a 30-60-90 triangle. Tangent is the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the side adjacent to the angle. Which of those sides is longer in a 30-60-90 triangle?

The side opposite the 60 degree angle is the longer one. So if I divide the longer side by the shorter side, I should get a number greater than 1. That means it has to be $\sqrt{3}$, right? Just say yes!

You have the right logic regarding the lengths of the sides and how that affects the ratio. If you apply the specific side length ratios for a 30-60-90 triangle—where the shortest side is 1 and the side opposite the 60 degree angle is $\sqrt{3}$—you will be able to finalize your answer.
Fine, I'll just do the division. Opposite is $\sqrt{3}$ and adjacent is 1, so $\sqrt{3}/1$ is just $\sqrt{3}$. I'm submitting it. Thanks I guess.
